      • literal

        @NonNull
public static Literal literal​(@Nullable
                              Object value)
        A literal term, as in WHERE k = 1.

        This method can process any type for which there is a default Java to CQL mapping, namely: primitive types (Integer=>int, Long=>bigint, String=>text, etc.), and collections, tuples, and user defined types thereof.

        A null argument will be rendered as NULL.

        For custom mappings, use literal(Object, CodecRegistry) or literal(Object, TypeCodec).

        Throws:
        com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.CodecNotFoundException - if there is no default CQL mapping for the Java type of value.

      • literal

        @NonNull
public static Literal literal​(@Nullable
                              Object value,
                              @NonNull
                              com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.registry.CodecRegistry codecRegistry)
        A literal term, as in WHERE k = 1.

        This is an alternative to literal(Object) for custom type mappings. The provided registry should contain a codec that can format the value. Typically, this will be your session's registry, which is accessible via session.getContext().getCodecRegistry().

        Throws:
        com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.CodecNotFoundException - if codecRegistry does not contain any codec that can handle value.
        See Also:
        AttachmentPoint.getCodecRegistry()

      • literal

        @NonNull
public static <T> Literal literal​(@Nullable
                                  T value,
                                  @Nullable
                                  com.datastax.oss.driver.api.core.type.codec.TypeCodec<T> codec)
        A literal term, as in WHERE k = 1.

        This is an alternative to literal(Object) for custom type mappings. The value will be turned into a string with TypeCodec.format(Object), and inlined in the query.

      • raw

        @NonNull
public static Raw raw​(@NonNull
                      String raw)
        A raw CQL snippet.

        The contents will be appended to the query as-is, without any syntax checking or escaping. This method should be used with caution, as it's possible to generate invalid CQL that will fail at execution time; on the other hand, it can be used as a workaround to handle new CQL features that are not yet covered by the query builder.
